newsitem.title: JAPAN: NEC sees 16 MB DRAM output at end-Dec below target.
newsitem.headline: NEC sees 16 MB DRAM output at end-Dec below target.

text.p: NEC Corp said on Monday that its output of 16 megabit dynamic random-access memory (DRAM) chips would grow to between 13 million and 14 million chips a month by the end of December.
The projected figure for the month to the end of December is up from current output of 11 million chips a month, though smaller than its original forecast.

An NEC spokesman said NEC had originally expected to make 18 million 16 megabit DRAM chips a month by the end of December, but earlier this year that was revised downward to 15 million to 16 million chips a month due to sluggish demand.
"Now, we think we will boost the output only to about 13 million to 14 million chips a month," he said.
He also said the company was considering investing less in semiconductors than it originally planned, but investment in the year to next March 31 would not fall below 200 billion yen.
The original investment goal for the 1996/97 business year was 210 billion yen.
